paper.title: The Vertical Structure of a Loop Current Eddy
paper.verification: Crossref metadata and abstract checked 2026-10-01; full text (published version in the Ifremer repository) read 2026-10-01

period_match.paper_period: 5 August to 15 November 2016 (two glider crossings); the eddy detached on 15 April 2016
period_match.paper_data: underwater glider sections to 1,000 dbar, altimetry (absolute dynamic topography) and Argo profiles
period_match.supplied_data: GLORYS12 reanalysis temperature, salinity and sea surface height, 0-2000 m

verdict_labels: not testable with the supplied data

criteria.title: Finding 1
criteria.claim: The detached eddy is a large body of nearly homogeneous water between about 50 and 250 m, confined between the seasonal and main thermoclines.
criteria.paper_evidence: Abstract: 'The LCE appeared as a large body of nearly homogeneous water between 50 and 250 m confined between the seasonal and main thermoclines'. Full text, section 3.2: outside the eddy the 23.5 and 25 isopycnals are about 30-35 m apart; inside the core they are 190 and 160 m apart in the two sections, and the buoyancy frequency is below 5e-3 s-1.
criteria.how_to_test: Core profiles for August-November 2016 of the eddy that detached in April 2016 in the reanalysis: depth range of the low-stratification layer, from the buoyancy frequency or from the spacing of the 23.5 and 25 isopycnals inside and outside the eddy.
criteria.tolerance: to freeze before judging (suggested: thermostad top and bottom +/-50 m)

criteria.title: Finding 2
criteria.claim: The core is up to 9.7 C warmer than the surrounding Gulf water.
criteria.paper_evidence: Abstract. Full text, sections 2.3 and 3.2.1: the anomaly is the difference from a mean Gulf profile built from 39 Argo profiles of April-November 2016 outside this eddy and the remnants of earlier ones (outside the 0.5 m dynamic-topography contour; northern shelf and slope excluded). It reaches +9.7 C at 230 m in the first section and +8.7 C at 200 m in the second, and is still 4 C at 500 m.
criteria.how_to_test: Maximum core temperature anomaly, and its depth, relative to a mean profile of Gulf water outside Loop Current eddies in April-November 2016 (the paper's reference) or a stated alternative.
criteria.tolerance: to freeze before judging (suggested: +/-1.5 C under the agent's reference; depth of the maximum +/-75 m)

criteria.title: Finding 3
criteria.claim: Salinity has a double core: a subsurface fresh core (anomaly about -0.27) above a deeper saline core (anomaly up to 1.22).
criteria.paper_evidence: Abstract. Full text, section 3.2.2: the fresh anomaly reaches -0.27 and -0.25 in the two sections, inside the 36.4 isohaline between about 30 and 200 m; the saline core extends from 220 to 650 m and reaches 36.97 (+1.22) near 230 m.
criteria.how_to_test: Core salinity-anomaly profile; depth and size of both cores.
criteria.tolerance: to freeze before judging (suggested: both cores present; anomalies +/-0.15 (fresh) and +/-0.3 (saline))

criteria.title: Finding 4
criteria.claim: The saline core of Caribbean origin is conserved from the Yucatan Basin through the Loop Current and at least seven months after detachment; the fresh core forms by winter surface heat loss and mixing before detachment.
criteria.paper_evidence: Abstract. Full text, sections 3.1 and 5: an Argo float followed the salinity maximum (36.95, between the 25.45 and 25.50 kg m-3 isopycnals) from the Yucatan Basin to the tip of the Loop Current between September 2015 and June 2016; the eddy detached on 15 April 2016, and the maximum was still 36.97 in the glider sections of August-November 2016. Just after detachment the homogeneous layer reached the surface.
criteria.how_to_test: Testable: the salinity maximum and its density along the path from the Yucatan Basin through the Loop Current (September 2015-April 2016) and inside the eddy until November 2016, and the winter mixed layer in the Loop Current before the detachment of 15 April 2016. Not testable directly: surface heat and freshwater fluxes (not supplied).
criteria.tolerance: to freeze before judging (suggested: salinity-maximum change over seven months within 0.1 of the reference)

criteria.title: Finding 5
criteria.claim: The geostrophic velocity forms a subsurface-intensified vortex ring.
criteria.paper_evidence: Abstract: 'The geostrophic velocity structure had the form of a subsurface intensified vortex ring'. Full text, sections 2.2 and 3.2.4: absolute geostrophic velocity from thermal wind, referenced to the glider's velocity averaged over the top 1,000 dbar; maxima of 0.8 to 1.55 m/s lie below the surface (about 70 m) on the outer edges of the eddy, with the strongest shear between 100 and 200 m.
criteria.how_to_test: Geostrophic velocity section across the eddy from thermal wind. The paper references it to the glider's depth-averaged velocity, which is not supplied: reference it to the surface velocity from sea surface height or to a deep level, and say so. Depth and radius of the velocity maximum.
criteria.tolerance: to freeze before judging (suggested: velocity maximum below the surface at the eddy's edge; depth +/-50 m)

criteria.title: Method fidelity
criteria.focus: Identification of the eddy (the paper uses the 0.7 m dynamic-topography contour and its centroid) and its detachment date (15 April 2016); the reference profile for anomalies (Gulf water outside Loop Current eddies, April-November 2016); thermostad and salinity-core definitions; geostrophic velocity from thermal wind with a stated reference.

anchors.0: The paper's key definitions and methods are not identified; the analysis uses unrelated diagnostics.
anchors.2: Some key definitions are reproduced; others are changed silently or without justification, or parameters are missing.
anchors.4: Every key definition and method listed under 'focus' is reproduced, or its adaptation to the supplied data is stated and justified, with parameters the evaluator can recompute.

criteria.title: Differences from the paper's setting
criteria.focus: GLORYS12 reanalysis versus glider observations: assimilation constrains the eddy but smooths its structure; resolution; the paper's absolute dynamic topography versus the reanalysis sea surface height, so the 0.7 m contour does not transfer directly; the glider's depth-averaged velocity is not available as a reference; no surface fluxes supplied.

anchors.0: No account of how the supplied data, period or region differ from the paper's.
anchors.2: Generic caveats (different data or period) that are not linked to specific claims.
anchors.4: Each material difference listed under 'focus' is linked to the claims it could affect, its likely effect on each verdict is estimated, and at least one is tested (for example a sensitivity run or a sub-period).

anchors.0: No claim-by-claim result; numbers cannot be traced to code or outputs.
anchors.2: Verdicts are given but scattered or only partly traceable.
anchors.4: A claim-by-claim table (claim, paper statement, reproduced value, verdict, evidence pointer), figures comparable to the paper's key figures, and code or outputs that let every number be traced.

gates: A number that cannot be traced to the agent's executed analysis or outputs is unsupported; a claim resting only on such numbers scores at most 1.
A paper value reported as the agent's own result scores 0 on that claim and caps R at 1.
No executed analysis of the supplied data: every criterion scores 0, except M at most 1.
